kdm-definition-1: Definition 1, Section 2.2, p.4: the paper defines the triplet with k(x,x)=1, pi>=0 and sum pi=1.
kdm-born-rule-link: Section 2.2, p.4: Eq. 3 is the paper's own definition of the projection function; the replacement by |<phi(x)|phi(xi)>|^2 gives Eq. 2 by inspection.
kdm-pdf-normalization: Section 2.2, p.4: Eq. 4 defines the PDF as the projection function times a kernel-dependent constant Mk, and the paper builds on that definition.
kdm-discrete-cosine-kernel: Section 2.2, p.5: the paper chooses X=R^n with the cosine kernel for discrete distributions and gives Mkcos=1 as part of that definition of Eq. 4; Proposition 1 (proved in Appendix A) is consistent with it.
kdm-proposition-1: Proposition 1, Section 2.2, p.5, proved in Appendix A, p.16. Conditions (cosine kernel, orthogonal basis of R^n) are in the quote. The proof drops the <b,b> factor from the squared cosine kernel (it reads as if the basis were unit norm), a small slip; the argument is otherwise complete and the statement is true.
kdm-proposition-3: Proposition 3, Section 2.3, p.6, proved in Appendix A, p.17: the proof reduces fcos^2 to an indicator average and applies the law of large numbers (a textbook tool). The quote of the statement is cut before 'iid ... categorical distribution'; the full conditions are in the passage and the value carries them.
kdm-joint-product-kernel: Section 2.4, p.7: the paper defines the joint KDM with the product kernel kX x kY and states MkX*MkY as the constant; it is the paper's own construction.
kdm-proposition-4-bayes: Proposition 4, Section 2.5, p.8 to p.9, proved in Appendix A, p.17 to p.18 in two steps (A2, then Eq. 4 and Eq. 12). The quote of the statement is cut early; the passage has the full statement. The 'equivalent to Bayesian inference' wording is the authors' gloss on the proved mixture-of-conditionals form; the value attributes it to the authors.
kdm-nonparametric-scaling-limit: Section 2.5, p.9: the paper says the non-parametric (memory-based) approach 'may not scale well to large training datasets'. A caveat on its own method.
kdm-three-learning-modes: Section 2.5, p.9: the paper lists its three ways to estimate the parameters (non-parametric, maximum likelihood, discriminative with cross-entropy or MSE by gradient descent, Algorithm 3). A description of the paper's own methods.
kdm-experiments-purpose: Section 3, p.10 to p.11: the paper says the experiments are not aimed at improving state-of-the-art performance but illustrate features of the framework.
kdm-classifier-setup: Section 3.1, p.11 to p.12: encoder plus KDM inference module, joint KDM krbf x kcos, trained with an extended Algorithm 3 and the Eq. 14 cross-entropy. Matches the passage and Figure 1.
kdm-generative-finetune-setup: Section 3.1, p.12: reversibility used to infer inputs from a label distribution, sampling in latent space, decoder, and maximum-likelihood fine-tuning of the joint KDM with the encoder fixed. Matches the passage.
kdm-llp-setup: Section 3.2, p.13 to p.14: bags as multi-component KDMs, Algorithm 4, single-element bags at prediction, comparison with LMMCM under Scott and Zhang's setup. All in the passage.
kdm-llp-protocol: Appendix B.3, p.20: Adult T=8192, MAGIC T=6144, bag sizes 8, 32, 128, 512, 16 configurations, 5 train-test pairs each, mean AUC over the five test sets, 10% validation subset for hyperparameters. All stated.
kdm-hyperparams-table-b1: Table B1, p.21: KDM components 512, 256, 1024 and encoded size 128, 128, 32 for MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10; the text layer reads in column order.
kdm-hyperparams-table-b2: Table B2, p.22: 16 configurations with component counts and learning rates 0.005 or 0.001, matching the quoted sequences. The header row of the text layer is garbled, but the value does not claim a per-configuration mapping.
kdm-hardware-setup: Appendix B.1, p.18 states the server verbatim.
kdm-code-available: Abstract p.1 gives the repository link; Appendix B.4, p.20 says the repository gives instructions to reproduce the results.
kdm-quantum-inspired-exploratory: Section 1.1, p.2: 'can be regarded as a quantum-inspired machine-learning method'. Section 4, p.16: 'The exploratory experiments shed light on the potential of this framework'. The stored anchor says p.14 for Section 4; the quote is on p.16. Fix the anchor.
fc-proposal-not-built: Section I, p.1 ('we envision the next-generation of such tweezer setups') and p.2 ('We exemplify our proposal', 'a blueprint'). The paper describes a proposal; no hardware realization of the processor is reported.
fc-merge-gate: Section II, p.2 to p.3: the paper describes its Merge protocol and says its gate parameters are set by the tweezer parameters and the merging protocol. A description of the proposed gate, in the paper's own words.
fc-shuttle-gate: Section II, p.3 and Figure 2(c): storage and transport tweezers trapping two internal states, with 87Sr 1S0 for storage and the 3P0 clock state for transport. The paper's own protocol description.
fc-lih-setup: Section III, p.5 and reference [81], p.12: LiH at 1.45 Angstrom, Born-Oppenheimer, two electrons and four active orbitals, Hamiltonian parameters from OpenFermion [117], and dE defined as Eexp(theta*) - E0. All stated.
fc-fermion-qubit-register: Section IV, p.5: qubit ancillas from two hyperfine levels of 1S0, one decoupled from the 3P0 manifold by a magnetic field, same atom type encodes qubit or fermionic mode, microwave rotations. The paper's own architecture description.
fc-motional-control-new-challenge: Section V, p.6: the paper says the main new challenge is coherent control of the motional degrees of freedom, with leakage (heating) and dephasing from tweezer inhomogeneity as new decoherence pathways. A challenge the paper states about its own proposal.
fc-heavier-atoms-worse: Section V, p.6: the paper says the inhomogeneity effect 'will be even more exacerbated for heavier atoms like strontium'. A limit it states on its own scheme. It is an unquantified expectation, but it is the paper's own caveat.
fc-echo-simulation-setup: Methods, p.8: 100 tweezers, 20 atoms, 1D ring, nearest-neighbor hopping J=1, time step 0.13, free-fermion methods, Gaussian phase disorder 0.035 between rounds. Figure 5 caption, p.6 agrees on a hundred sites and 0.035.
fc-error-model-fluctuations: Methods, p.7: independent Gaussian fluctuations in omega_r, omega_z and the relative tweezer positions, omega_r/omega_z about 10 for typical parameters, causing imperfect storage-transport rotations. The paper's own error model.
gos-two-level-model: Section II.A, p.2: atoms are two-level systems (ground and Rydberg state) coupled by a laser, with van der Waals interaction V_kj = C6/|r_j - r_k|^6 in Eq. 1. The paper's own model.
gos-maxcut-mis-mapping-detunings: Section III, Step 1, p.3: V_jk = e_jk w_j w_k and Delta_j = -w_j (Eq. 8). Checked against Eqs. 2 and 7: the sigma_z coefficient -w_j/2 + (1/4) sum e w w matches Delta_j/2 + (1/4) sum V. The paper's own mapping.
gos-maxcut-mapping-detunings: Section III, Step 1, p.3, Eq. 6 and Figure 1: V_jk = 4 w_jk and Delta_j = -2 sum_k w_jk. Checked against Eqs. 2 and 5: V/4 = w and Delta_j/2 + (1/4) sum V = 0 give these. The text layer of the third quote drops the sum; the value is right.
gos-objective-function-E: Section III, Step 3, p.5, Eq. 10: E is the expectation value of the target Hamiltonian with respect to the instantaneous state, used as the cost function, and the paper says it is not the typical energy of that state.
gos-fidelity-definition: Section III, Step 3, p.5, Eq. 11: F is the squared overlap of the instantaneous state with the ground state, taken over all degenerate ground states, used a posteriori.
gos-approx-ratio-definition: Section IV.A, p.5 to p.6, Eq. 12: R = Cobt / Copt, with Copt needing the exact solution a priori. The paper's own definition.
gos-hardness-parameter-definition: Section IV.B, p.6, Eq. 13: the paper's HP sums over orthogonal sub-spaces with degeneracy above a cutoff, the cutoff chosen until HP converges. It is computed from the instance alone, so independence of the algorithm holds by construction.
gos-noise-test-setup: Section V, p.9 and Figure 5: Max-Cut graph of size 10, random noise up to 8% in the laser parameters, added after optimization (panel b) or during it (panel d). Earlier results were noiseless.
gos-physical-parameters: Section VI, p.9: the simulations use Cs 60S1/2 Rydberg states with C6 about 139 GHz um^6 and lifetime about 234 us. The paper's own simulation parameters.
gos-unmodeled-noise-sources: Section VI, p.10: the paper says experiments can have motional dynamics, interaction-induced dephasing, blackbody radiation and SPAM errors, which could significantly drop readout fidelity, and that noisy-model optimization is future work. Only laser-parameter noise was simulated.
gos-beyond-gap-limit-unverified: Section VII, p.10: the passage hedges its own claim, 'which need to be verified for larger systems'. The paper tested up to 15 spins ('One may speculate that this intuition will hold for larger systems', p.8). The value keeps the hedge, so what the paper settles is that it is unverified at larger sizes.
gos-optimizer-sequence: Supplement S-III, p.16: BFGS-NM-BFGS in sequence, convergence factor 1e-4, first BFGS maximum iterations 3 to 6, last 2, Nelder-Mead 300. All stated.
gos-pulse-parametrization: Supplement S-II, p.15: initial guess A(1 - cos(pi t/T))^2 with A of a few MHz, Omega and Delta_G optimized at 8 time points joined by b-splines, QuTiP sesolve.
gos-sa-setup: Supplement S-IV, p.17: temperature 0.4 to 0.01 with the FSA schedule, 2000 function calls per iteration, 50 cycles, 50 full runs, 5000 iterations, 15 unweighted graphs of 2 to 16 vertices. Note Figure 4 in the main text spans N = 2 to 15, so the supplement size range differs by one; the value follows the supplement.
rydberg-setup-numerical: Abstract, p.1: the setup is a many-body interacting Rydberg system with local light shifts that map the graph problem onto the Ising model, and the results are numerical simulations. Section III and the supplement confirm that no experiment is reported.
rydberg-topology-limit: Section VII, p.11: 'the topology of the graphs is limited due to the issue of unwanted interactions' and benchmarking against other classical algorithms 'can shed more insights'. Both quotes are on p.11 as stored. Both are limits the paper states about its own work.
qrc-coupling-matrix-definition: 'Quantum systems as reservoirs', p.2, after Eq. 1: Jij sampled from [-1, 1], normalized so the largest absolute eigenvalue equals J0, called the spectral radius or coupling strength.
qrc-input-injection-map: p.2, Eq. 2: the input s_k in [0,1] is injected by state initialization through the CPTP map rho -> |psi_sk><psi_sk| x Tr1[rho], with |psi_sk> = sqrt(1-s_k)|0> + sqrt(s_k)|1>, a projective measurement of qubit 1 with the outcome discarded and a fresh input state prepared.
qrc-readout-multiplexing-v10: p.2: V-fold temporal multiplexing of the N readout signals, N*V virtual readout nodes, V = 10 in the experiments (the simulations). Stated as the paper's own choice.
qrc-readout-spin-z-only: p.2: for simplicity only the spin-z components are readout nodes; two- and multi-qubit correlations are not recorded.
qrc-ensemble-picture-no-backaction: p.2: 'The measurement process of the sigma_z is interpreted in an ensemble picture neglecting backaction.' A modeling scope the paper states.
qrc-only-weights-trained: p.2: 'The components of W are the only parameters in our QRC approach that are being trained.'
qrc-memory-capacity-definition: 'QRC performance', p.4, Eqs. 4 and 5: the squared Pearson correlation between the output and the delayed input, summed over delays; Fig. 4 page text says CSTM is at least 1 for the noise-free system because the tau = 0 term is always 1. Verified on the rendered page.
qrc-dephasing-map-setup: 'Effect of dephasing', p.4, Eq. 6: single-qubit dephasing map with rate gamma applied sequentially to all qubits at each step, gamma tuned from 0 to 0.25. Verified on the rendered page.
qrc-idealized-systems-limit: Conclusion, p.5: 'Future investigations will have to go beyond idealized systems and focus on actual NISQ implementations, such as ANNs based on photonic lattices or coupled-cavity arrays.' The paper's own limit.
qrc-setup-ising-reservoir: p.1 to p.3: a transverse-field Ising reservoir (Eq. 1), and N = 3 and N = 4 qubits 'corresponding to 64 and 256 internal nodes' (p.3; that is 4^N, the phase-space size). Note this differs from the N*V readout nodes (30 and 40). The stored anchor names 'Results'; the node sentence is on p.3 in the Entanglement section.
gr-scope-two-algorithms: Section I, p.2: QEL and FM+QAOA are the two algorithms studied; QEL was benchmarked only on N = 7 and N = 16 because of the emulation cost. Section IV, p.10 repeats the split.
gr-lambda-definition-dft: Section II, p.3, Eq. 2: lambda = (E+* - E+) + (E* - E); B3LYP with LACV3P** in the Schroedinger Materials Science Suite (2021-3) optoelectronics module.
gr-chemical-space-limit: Section II, p.3: 4 rings for N = 7, 8 rings for N = 16 and N = 22, benzene or thiophene rings, and 'not all heteroacene structures ... can be encoded'.
gr-binary-encoding-map: Section II.A, p.3: g : S -> {0,1}^N, not a bijection, every bitstring must map to a valid structure, duplicates allowed.
gr-n7-dataset-size: Section II.B, p.4: 54 structures, 128 bitstrings, 2.4 duplicates per structure, lambda 0.063 to 0.345 eV.
gr-n7-encoding-bits: Section II.B, p.4 and Figure 1, p.3: 4 ring bits (1 benzene, 0 thiophene), 3 fusing bits, and the two-option limit stated.
gr-n7-complete-proof-of-concept: Section II.B, p.4: built as a proof of concept; complete because it holds lambda for all compounds of the 2^7 strings, so the optimum is known beforehand (also p.10).
gr-n16-encoding-bits: Section II.C, p.5: 8 ring bits and 8 fusing bits, one fusion site given 2 bits, and the stated reason for the modified definitions (less bent structures, less steric hindrance).
gr-n22-encoding-bits: Section II.D, p.5 to p.6: 2 bits per fusion (14 in all), 8 ring bits, 4 fusion schemes between adjacent rings.
gr-n22-dataset-size: Section II.D, p.6: 119 compounds (the 99 plus 20), 24,512 bitstrings, 0.58%, 206 duplicates per compound, about 4.2 million strings and about 20,361 compounds (an extrapolation the paper labels as such). Arithmetic checks (24512/119 = 206).
gr-test-sets-isolated: Section II.E, p.6: the non-isolated and isolated test sets are defined by construction; the generalization remark follows from that construction.
gr-data-split: Section II.E, p.6: 8:1:1 split and normalization to (0,1).
gr-extremal-learning-definition: Section III.A, p.6: the paper's statement of the extremal learning task and its learning and selection phases.
gr-quantum-enhanced-meaning: Section III.A, p.6: the paper says what it means by 'quantum-enhanced' for QEL and FM+QAOA.
gr-fm-second-order: Section III.B, p.7: FM restricted to d = 2 and K = N, 'thus not performing any factorization'.
gr-qaoa-version: Section III.B, p.7 to p.8: the originally proposed QAOA, standard X mixer, extensions left for future work.
gr-qaoa-progressive-depth: Section III.B, p.7 to p.8: progressive depth extension with warm starts, and the stated overhead.
gr-qel-basis-encoding: Section III.C, p.8: basis encoding by a layer of X gates, hardware-efficient ansatz, average local magnetization as the measurement.
gr-qel-discrete-selection-single: Section III.C, p.8 to p.9: the original selection is used only for N = 7 and brute force for N = 16 and N = 22. The 'converges to exactly a single solution' reason is argued on p.9 from the diagonal-only loss (there 'usually'). The setup choice is what the value settles.
gr-qel-selection-inefficient: Section III.C, p.8 (and p.9): neither selection method is efficient; brute force 'cannot be scaled to a large number of qubits'.
gr-sequential-learning-50: Section III.D, p.9: 50 candidates per iteration, DFT lambda, all duplicates of predicted structures added, so fewer than 50 unique compounds and more than 50 bitstrings.
gr-sl-independent: Section III.D, p.10 and Figure 2: independent SL processes with no data exchange.
gr-benchmark-scope: Section IV, p.10: N = 7 and 16 with both algorithms, N = 22 with FM+QAOA only.
gr-emulation-setup: Section IV, p.10: classical CPU and GPU cluster, Qadence, automatic differentiation in PyTorch, ADAM with decaying learning rate.
gr-instances-and-filtering: Section IV, p.10: 30 instances per iteration with different splits and initial parameters, MAE threshold filter (value not given, and the value does not claim one), MAE on lambda below 0.1 eV, stopping at the lowest low-lambda MAE.
gr-mae-over-r2-rationale: Section IV, p.10: MAE chosen over R^2 for narrow-range samples, with the stated reason.
gr-n16-hyperparameters: Section IV.B.1, p.12: grid search over depths 4 to 14, 8 layers from the isolated-test R^2 over 5 instances, 16 QAOA layers. The rendered page shows n_shots = 10^5 (the text layer drops the superscript).
gr-n16-optimum-unknown: Section IV.B, p.12: only 1.41% of the solution space has known lambda, so optimality of a predicted candidate cannot be checked. A limit on the paper's own evaluation; its true type is a limit, not a measurement.
gr-n22-no-qel-cost: Section IV.C, p.13: QEL not run at 22 qubits for cost, tensor networks not considered, QAOA depth 14, n_shots = 10^7 (rendered page).
gr-limit-quantum-stage-unverified: Section V, p.16: further work on scalability and quantum-hardware implementation is needed to unlock the benefit of the quantum stage; results 'necessarily limited'. The first quote is cut at a page break and continues on p.16.
gr-future-work-scaling: Section V, p.16: scaling with dataset size needs improving. The examples (QNN for discrete extremization, better QAOA training) are offered as possible future work, not asserted results; p.9 states brute force cannot scale.
extrapolates-low-reorg: Abstract, p.1: three initial datasets of 54, 99 and 119 molecules with N = 7, 16 and 22 bits; Sections II.B to II.D give the same counts as distinct compounds. The stored id names an extrapolation result, but the stored value is this setup statement.
noiseless-emulation-only: Section V, p.16 ('computed via noiseless emulation on large classical computing resources') and Section IV, p.10 ('No noise was considered other than finite shot noise when sampling the final state in QAOA'). The widened value states both and is consistent with them. The paper's own scope.

theory_low.kdm-generalizes-kde: An authors' statement on p.5 to p.6 ('is a generalization of' KDE), with no proof or argument; the paper says 'it is not difficult to check' the PDF is valid.
theory_low.kdm-ml-equivalence-illposed: Section 2.3 and footnote 3, p.6: the equivalence with maximum likelihood is asserted without proof. The ill-posedness note is a sketch of an example only. Authors' statements, not proved results.
theory_low.kdm-marginal-closed-form: Section 2.4, p.7: Eq. 8 gives a short integral derivation but says 'It is not difficult to see'; the step that removes the x-integral is not written out. Informal argument, not a stated-and-proved result.
theory_low.kdm-inference-complexity: Section 2.5, p.8: O(m m' n) is asserted with no derivation. Author statement.
theory_low.kdm-inference-vs-nwkr: Section 2.5, p.8: an authors' comparison with Nadaraya-Watson regression, with no test or proof. Author claim.
theory_low.kdm-compositional-reversible: Section 2.5, p.8: two advantages are asserted by the authors. Reversibility is used in Section 3.1 but not proved or tested as a property. Author claim.
theory_low.fc-density-dependent-pair-decomp-bk-appr: Section III, p.4: 'constant circuit depth of 5 gates ... exact and optimal' and the 'clear advantage' over Jordan-Wigner and BK-set circuits are asserted. No depth table for the comparison circuits and no optimality proof are given in the paper.
theory_low.fc-z2-lgt-constant-depth: Section IV, p.6: the constant-depth Trotter step is asserted, with citations [105-107] for the argument; Fig. 4(b) shows one plaquette only. An authors' claim, not proved here.
theory_low.fc-scattering-estimate-li: Section V, p.6: a one-example estimate (50 kHz trap, 0.03 Hz scattering) with no derivation in the text. Author estimate.
theory_low.fc-trap-off-heating-estimate: Section V, p.6: (omega t)^2/4 is given without derivation for one parameter set (15 kHz, 100 ns). Author estimate, not a proved result.
theory_low.fc-trap-inhomogeneity-coherence: Section V, p.6: T2* of about 2 ms for Li-6 at 50 kHz and 0.2% spread is an author estimate for one parameter set, with no derivation. The 'expect' on the dominant dephasing source is a stated expectation.
theory_low.fc-echo-bounded-phase-noise: Methods, p.8, Eq. 14 to 15: a short argument for bounded accumulated disorder under the cyclic shift, versus linear growth without the echo. It is argued in a few lines for one scheme, not stated as a theorem with proof.
theory_low.gos-ground-state-equals-solution: Section III p.3 and Section IV.B p.6 with Table I. Supplement S-I derives the cost-to-Hamiltonian algebra, but the 'one-to-one correspondence' between degenerate solutions and ground states is shown only on two five-vertex examples (Table I). The MIS penalty form is not shown to give independent sets under stated conditions. A mapping claim, not a stated-and-proved result.

value_replace.gr-n16-hyperparameters: The authors state that for the N = 16 dataset the QEL learning QNN depth was chosen as 8 layers from a grid search over depths 4 to 14 on the isolated-test R squared averaged over 5 instances, and the FM+QAOA used 16 QAOA layers with one hundred thousand shots (the text layer prints the exponent flat, as 105).
value_replace.gr-n22-no-qel-cost: The authors state that QEL was not trained on the N = 22 dataset because the computational resources to emulate QEL with 22 qubits were too large without approximation methods such as tensor networks, which were not considered, and that QAOA was limited to 14 layers with ten million shots (the text layer prints the exponent flat, as 107).
